reader.requirement: At --std 85 the SOURCE-COMPUTER computer-name must be a system-name: a COBOL word of at most 30 characters drawn from A-Z (lowercase equivalent), 0-9 and hyphen, hyphen neither first nor last, and not a 1985 reserved word (reserved words and system-names are disjoint; LENGTH, RANDOM and SUM never system-names); a literal, a numeric literal, a figurative constant, an underscore or extended letter must be refused, while a 1985 function-name or a word reserved only in later editions must be accepted.

edition-consulted.switches: which words are reserved (the R85 column at --std 85: MEMORY, MODULES, WORDS, SEGMENT-LIMIT reserved; TYPEDEF, ARITHMETIC not)
token-level reservation gate via ReservedWordSet.AdmitsAsUserWord at the edition: a later-reserved word becomes an IDENTIFIER at 85
COBOL0901 for a word reserved at the edition (RejectsAt(word, edition.Year))
word length limit 30 at 85, 31 at 2002/2014, 63 at 2023
underscore gate user-word-underscore-2002 and extended-letter gate (COBOL0900 at 85)
WITH DEBUGGING MODE without computer-name gated as computer-name-optional-2002

refuter.evidence: The reader's requirement leaves out a part of the 1985 definition of system-name that SR1 depends on. §1985:IV.4.2.2.1.2 says 'There are three types of system-names: 1. computer-name 2. implementor-name 3. language-name. Within a given implementation these three types of system-names form disjoint sets; a given system-name may belong to one and only one of them.' (cite.py: OK  §1985:IV.4.2.2.1.2  (4.2.2.1.2 System-Names)  the text is in the clause; OK  §1985:VI.4.3.3 SR1  (4.3.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR1). This implementation's implementor-names (src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Editions/ImplementorNames.cs: CONSOLE, SYSIN, SYSOUT, SYSERR, C01, CSP, SWITCH-0..36, UPSI-0..7; code-names ASCII, EBCDIC in ImplementorCodeNames.cs) are therefore not computer-names at 1985, so 'SOURCE-COMPUTER. CONSOLE.' names no computer-name. Probes at --std 85 (refute-1985-049/src/sysn/s-*.cob): CONSOLE, SYSIN, SYSOUT, SYSERR, C01, CSP, EBCDIC, ASCII, SWITCH-1, UPSI-0 as the computer-name all give EXIT 0 RAN. r2-console-both2.cob uses CONSOLE as the SOURCE-COMPUTER and OBJECT-COMPUTER computer-name AND as implementor-name-1 (CONSOLE IS MYCON, DISPLAY UPON MYCON) in one program: EXIT 0 RAN, so one word belongs to two of the three disjoint sets. The parts the reader did cover hold: every one of the 350 words in the 1985 reserved-word list (§1985:IV.8, which matches the R85 column of ReservedWords.Table.cs exactly, 350 = 350) was compiled as the SOURCE-COMPUTER computer-name (src/w85/s-*.cob, results in src/w85-results.txt), and all 350 were refused with EXIT 65.
edition-sites-missed: src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Frontend/Grammar/CobolParserCore.g4#computerName: cobolWord with no screen against the implementor system-name table at any edition; 1985 needs a disjointness arm (2023 §8.3.2.3.1 lists only device-name, feature-name and switch-name as mutually exclusive, so at 2023 the same acceptance is not a fault)
src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Editions/ImplementorNames.cs#(table): the 1985 implementor-names a computer-name must not be; not consulted on the computer-name path
refuter.corrected: PARTIAL (harm: under-rejects; cause a/c: 1985 needs its own arm). The reserved-word, character-set and length parts conform, but at --std 85 a computer-name spelled as one of this implementation's implementor-names (CONSOLE, SYSIN, SYSOUT, SYSERR, C01, CSP, SWITCH-n, UPSI-n, ASCII, EBCDIC) is accepted. §1985:IV.4.2.2.1.2 makes computer-names and implementor-names disjoint sets within an implementation, so this should be refused. Minimal repro: SOURCE-COMPUTER. CONSOLE. with SPECIAL-NAMES. CONSOLE IS MYCON. At --std 85 it gives EXIT 0 RAN; expected a refusal. At --std 2023 it also gives EXIT 0 RAN, which is correct there because 2023 removed computer-name from the exclusive types. Known note: none found (grep of kb/Work for disjoint/computer-name/implementor-name). The sibling pattern, 1985 disjoint sets not enforced, is PB5482 (text-names and library-names). The docs docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-127.md ('accepted with any spelling') and DOC-A.1-198.md, which document the any-spelling rule, would need a 1985 exception.

CONSOLE.` runs in a program that also uses CONSOLE as an implementor-name; 1985 makes the computer-names and the implementor-names of an implementation disjoint sets. The checker rates this medium: the sentence is about the implementation's name sets, not a syntax rule on programs.
